tasks.title: Impact dust lands on raw ground, ignoring the man's own drawn height
tasks.why: CombatFx.cs:758-768 (the new feet Spurt in the Hit case, from bdfed04ff/the review 2026-10-12): `feet = (p.x, RenderGround.Sample(Host.Local.Map, p.x, p.z), p.z)` throws away `p.y` outright and resamples raw terrain height. `p` itself can come from `units.Sockets(e.B, ...)`, the figure's real drawn chest position, which may sit above bare terrain (a man on a trench fire-step, a bridge, a roof prop); EstimateChest's fallback already uses the same ground sample, but the socketed case does not. The dust puff then draws at bare-ground level, floating above or sunk below the man's actual feet, and in water it draws dry dust under the surface instead of a splash. No existing test exercises a socketed hit on raised ground. P2.
tasks.done_when: a test with units.Sockets returning a chest position above RenderGround.Sample's height for that x/z asserts the Spurt's y tracks the socketed height (or its offset from it), not the raw ground sample alone
